svg.title: A nurse on a medical unit is assessing a 68-year-old client who has a peripheral IV in the left forearm infusing 0.9% sodium chloride. The skin around the site is cool, pale, and puffy, the skin feels taut, and the pump keeps alarming for occlusion. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
svg.desc: COOL AND PALE AND SWOLLEN AND TAUT = INFILTRATION, so fluid is leaking into tissue and the catheter must come out; elevating the arm helps reabsorption and the new site goes in the OTHER arm. Flushing or milking pushes more fluid into the tissue and worsens injury. Continuing the infusion at any rate keeps damaging tissue, and a compress is only useful AFTER the catheter is removed.
